brief.scope:
Fix-round review of PR #242 (lane/session-20260916-d, head e0e0b732), fresh round after the first (records 20260916T075500Z-review-grok-c7a708, 20260916T075518Z-review-codex-c22c2d), whose 11 accepted findings this head answers in fix commit 65967fa8, one Finding/Verified pair per finding: the server renamed to coordination, placement engine none, the seam settled against the core at 05b8aebe on lane/session-20260916-c via the CORE table with reader and writer store handles, refusals on resources/read as JSON-RPC error objects carrying the wire line, an explicit tool-to-verb table.
Check each fix against its finding: is any accepted finding only partly fixed; do the 11 new test cases pin the fixed behaviour itself, not just the words used to describe it.

findings.claim: X#3 is only partly fixed. bounded() caps the verb payload at 16384 bytes; tools/call then serialises that payload twice (content.text and structuredContent), so a 12000-byte payload becomes a 24134-byte JSON-RPC response, and _send itself is still uncapped. The original reproduce still writes 70009 bytes. test_a_payload_over_the_bound_answers_the_unavailable_reading exercises CLI call, not serve. test_every_paged_read_carries_an_explicit_cursor only asserts that tools/list schema contains the key cursor; it never calls a paged tool or checks that a cursor reached the core.
findings.reproduce: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'ops/conductor/tools'); import coordination_mcp as m; m._send({'x':'x'*70000})" | wc -c

findings.claim: G#5 is only partly fixed. The duplicate 2.3 heading was split and a hermetic session row was added, but Precedence still says that with no binding, mutations refuse class identity and reads that carry no participant-specific content still answer. The new registry row and no-binding-at-all case refuse class session on coord_brief, a read; a mutation with no binding also refuses session, never identity.
findings.reproduce: env -u CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID -u CLAUDE_SESSION_ID python3 -B ops/conductor/tools/coordination_mcp.py call coord_brief; env -u CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID -u CLAUDE_SESSION_ID python3 -B ops/conductor/tools/coordination_mcp.py call coord_submit '{"assignment":"A-1","evidence":"abc1234","revision":"abc1234","generation":1}'; sed -n '182,187p' ops/conductor/coordination-mcp-lever.md

findings.claim: The seam case named for reader and writer store handles does not pin that the handle reaches the verb, nor that a mutation receives writer(). It calls coord_brief only and reads participant.store, which the stub's bound_participant copies from its conn argument; stub verbs ignore conn. writer() is planted and never asserted. A projection that passed reader() to the resolver and a different handle to the verb, or reader() for every tool, would keep this case green.

The G#4/X#6 case pins the remedy sentence, not the G#4 reproduce. Unauthorized coord_observe with {"role":"lead"} still refuses class arguments, so the caller still learns the forbidden-argument table. That call is not in the suite; the new case uses no arguments and asserts the substring "arguments are checked once the capability is held".
